title: As AI agents reshape the web, Google opens Gemini and Search to more apps
slides: Can Google keep the web open as AI agents take over?
Gemini and Search now connect to more third-party apps
But agents may bypass the open web entirely
Developers must rethink how content gets discovered
Ask: who controls the agent's attention tomorrow?
thread_text:
1. The web's gatekeeper problem

Google's Gemini and Search now plug into third-party apps. That's convenience for users, but it means the door to the web is increasingly owned by one company.

2. Agents skip the open web

AI agents can pull answers straight from apps and APIs. Why browse a website when your assistant already has the data?

3. Discovery breaks down

If agents bypass the open web, developers lose the traffic that made the web a business. SEO becomes AI optimization, or nothing.

4. Rethinking discovery

Developers now have to design for machine readers, not just humans. Structured data and agent-friendly APIs matter more than keywords.

5. Who owns attention?

Ask yourself: if an agent chooses what you see, who really controls your attention? Try simulating one task with an AI agent today and see what it skips.
